# Lessons by aspect

Lessons for large engineering work done with AI agents, drawn from the case studies in [the case index](../index.md). Each lesson is one line in our own words with a stable ID (the prefix names its page), the cases behind it, the evidence against it, and whether it needs the old system as its oracle. The [checklist](../checklist.md) cites lessons by ID. This page is a table of contents: to choose lessons, read [evidence.md](evidence.md) (one line per lesson), then open an aspect page only for the lessons you use.

Evidence base: every lesson here comes from the **migrations** in [this collection](../index.md), all done with AI except one rule-based contrast case; many apply to large engineering work done with AI agents generally.

The legend of the tags, the Era and the strength rule heads every aspect page.

## May be outdated

"May be outdated" marks a lesson about what models can or cannot do (tagged "Depends on model ability: yes") whose most recent case (the later of its publication date and the end of its work) is more than 12 months older than the newest update in the log: newer models may no longer behave so; re-check it against recent work before you rely on it.

- **TOL-2** ([Rule-based tools and AI](tooling.md)) Run a rule-based codemod first and give the model its partial output, with a note wherever the rules gave up; it anchors the model.
- **AGF-8** ([Agent failure modes](agent-failures.md)) Check how well the model handles each language in scope; one poorly supported language fell back to people.

## By model

With a specific or a new model: process lessons (model ability: no) apply as they are. Start with the lessons tagged yes or partly whose cases name your model or its family ("By model" in lessons/index.md); treat those from other models as things to re-check on yours, not tips. A model released after the newest case (published 2026-11-03) has no evidence here yet. The lessons hold only what the cases show: no prompting advice.

Families group the model names the cases give by maker, line and major version ("Claude Opus 4.6" and "Opus 4.8" are Claude Opus 4.x; "GPT-5.4" and "gpt-5.5" are GPT-5.x); a name with a line but no version, and an internal model, stay apart; unstated covers the cases that name no model. Lessons: those tagged yes or partly for model ability whose cited cases name a model of the family (a lesson's Era names only the newest). Newest case: the latest publication date among the cases that name it. Families with the same newest case and lessons share a row.
